newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds up in light trade after FOMC.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds up in light trade after FOMC.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities rose with Treasuries on Tuesday after the Federal Reserve ended its Federal Open Market Committee meeting with no change in monetary policy.
Traders reported light activity in pass-throughs during the first hour after the Fed's policy meeting.
"We haven't done a trade since that effect came into play," one trader said.
Late on Tuesday, pass-throughs were up 4/32 to 8/32 overall, while the 10-year Treasury note had climbed 13/32 to yield 6.76 percent.
Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0 percent coupons were up 5/32 at 100-18/32, yielding 119 basis points. Comparable Fannie Maes had risen 7/32, and Freddie Mac's were up 6/32.

CMOs saw more activity, with bid lists circulating through the structured-product arena late on Tuesday morning, traders said. Some investors moved to unwind short positions ahead of the Fed's announcement, they said.

"Short money-market stuff" made the rounds, one trader said. Some investors who had been counting on a Fed tightening apparently changed their minds, "and they wanted to get out of those positions before the Fed made a statement," he said.
